lesson.title: Bingo de Números: Cero to Treinta
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: This week you learned to count, listen, do math, and use real numbers — landmarks, tricky teens, twenties, and treinta. Today you'll put it all to the test in number bingo, cero to treinta.

In today's bingo, a caller says un número between cero and treinta, and everyone checks their board for a match. Make your board with numerals, not words — that keeps it a real listening challenge, not a reading one.

How to play: make a bingo board and fill it with numerals of your choice from 0-30. Take turns being the caller: the caller picks a number, says it out loud in Spanish (using this week's landmark chant to double check any tricky ones), and everyone covers that numeral if it's on their board. First to cover a full row says ¡Bingo!

Being the caller is extra practice too — you have to convert a numeral you see into the Spanish word out loud, the reverse direction of Tuesday's dictation. If you get stuck on a number, use Monday's landmark chant to find your place: is it just past quince? Just before veinte?

You just spent a full week living inside Spanish numbers — from a seven-number landmark chant on Monday to a full bingo game today. Next week you'll keep counting, all the way up to cien — one hundred!

questions.explanation: Treinta is a fresh new word for 30 — no gluing.
Veinticinco is one of your landmark numbers — 25.

objectives: Convert a numeral on a bingo board into its spoken Spanish word, cero through treinta
Use the landmark chant to place an unfamiliar number during live play
Play both caller and listener roles in a full week-ending review game
materialsNeeded: Family members or classmates to play with
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Explain today's game: number bingo, cero to treinta, with the whole family able to play.
2. Have each player draw a grid and fill it with numerals of their choice from 0-30.
3. Take turns being the caller: pick a numeral, say it aloud in Spanish, and let players cover a match.
4. When stuck on a number, pause and use Monday's landmark chant together to place it.
5. Play until someone completes a row and calls ¡Bingo!
6. Complete the review activity together.
7. Complete the worksheet, recapping the whole week.
8. Preview next week: numbers 31-100.
differentiationTips: Struggling: build a bingo board using only landmark numbers (cero, cinco, diez, quince, veinte, veinticinco, treinta) plus a few teens, rather than the full 0-30 range
Ready for more: let them be the caller for the whole game, converting every numeral on the board into its spoken Spanish word without checking the chant first

This lesson relies on a parent, teacher, or classmate calling numbers aloud rather than an audio recording, since the course doesn't have audio content yet (open decision, expansion-plan-2026-09.md §12.9) — the printed numeral-to-word answer key covers the same ground a recording would for checking calls
teacherGuide.answerKey: Bingo numerals are read aloud using this week's rules: individual names through catorce, diez+y+digit for 16-19, veinte+y+digit for 21-29, and the landmarks cero, cinco, diez, quince, veinte, veinticinco, treinta. Dieciocho=18, veintitrés=23, veinticinco=25 (a landmark), treinta=30.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Closes the week's WA-WL-2015.3.1 Connections arc with an authentic, repeated real-world-style task (calling and covering numbers under time pressure) rather than a single scripted exchange, mirroring week 3's Day 5 pattern of a live, unscored performance task that recombines everything taught that week.
